title: Drivers' Hours Cheat Sheet
summary: Every drivers' hours and working time limit for lorry drivers, on two pages.

items.label: daily driving (10 h twice a week)

rows: At least 45 minutes, or at least 15 then at least 30
9 hours, up to 10 hours twice in a fixed week
11 hours, or split 3 + 9 hours (12 in total)
At least 9 hours, up to 3 times between weekly rests
45 hours, or reduced to at least 24 hours
No later than six 24-hour periods after the last one
notes: A reduced weekly rest must be made up in one block before the end of the third week after it.

blocks.title: The split break trap
blocks.text: A split break must be at least 15 minutes first and at least 30 minutes second. 30 then 15 doesn't count as a full break.

pages.heading: GB domestic rules and working time

rows: Weekly record sheet when driving over 4 hours a day (operator licence vehicles)
notes: Used by most goods vehicles exempt from the assimilated rules.

blocks.title: Breaks under working time
items: Working 6 to 9 hours: breaks totalling at least 30 minutes.
Working more than 9 hours: breaks totalling at least 45 minutes.
Each break should be at least 15 minutes.
Breaks and periods of availability don't count as working time.
Working time records are kept for 2 years.

blocks.title: Duty isn't driving
blocks.text: Under GB domestic rules, the 10-hour limit counts only driving. The 11-hour limit counts all duty: driving and all other work, but not rest or breaks.

sources.doc: GOV.UK: Drivers' hours and tachographs: goods vehicles (GV262)
